Not an expert, but I do a lot of travel. So I'll throw a couple semi-scientific things and anecdotes in here, and maybe an expert can clean them up.

But first, there's a lot of things that dictate how awake/tired you feel, beyond how much sleep you get. Normal sleep pattern is huge in this regard. If you're used to a 5 o'clock nap, it's probably going to hit you every day, no matter how much you sleep.

Eating habits also impact need for sleep. Your meal schedule is one of the most important factors in altering sleep schedule, especially for long-distance travel. A fairly-recent study found that in people who were traveling, those that adjusted their meal schedule early also adjusted their sleep schedule more quickly. So if you're headed to Europe from America, eat breakfast at 1am (assuming you're jumping ahead 8hrs). Then eat lunch at 4/5am, etc. This gets your body doing what it needs to be doing. I'm oblivious to the science behind it though. Sorry about that.

And finally, it's very easy to gradually slip around the clock if you don't have a set sleep schedule. I once had a friend who was on scholarship and was taking no classes that semester. He kept going to bed later and waking up earlier. Over the course of the semester, he slipped entirely around the clock until his sleep schedule was normalized again. Fun stuff.

Check out Sleep Cycles. You are probably not lining up with the correct cycle. Also your body gets used to certain sleep and awake times. We don't exactly turn OFF and ON like a computer. There is a process that our bodies go through such as producing melatonin.
